key_insight: In Saudi paediatric ASD reports, atypical antipsychotics showed drug- and age-specific safety signals, with the strongest signals varying by agent and organ system.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help clinicians and pharmacovigilance teams watch more closely for adverse reactions in children, especially younger age groups, when using atypical antipsychotics.
method: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of SFDA pharmacovigilance reports from 2021-2024.
Included 701 paediatric ADR reports (ages 0-19 years) and assessed sex/age patterns.
Used disproportionality methods: ROR, PRR, and BCPNN, with Firth logistic regression for association checks.
evidence_signal: Signals included nervous system disorders with risperidone, cardiac/general disorders with quetiapine, haematological/metabolic/psychiatric disorders with olanzapine, and gastrointestinal disorders with aripiprazole.
watch_item: Spontaneous reporting data can show disproportionality but cannot prove causality, and underreporting or reporting bias may affect interpretation.
paper_title: Evaluating the Real-World Safety of Atypical Antipsychotics in Paediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder: Lessons from Saudi Arabia's Pharmacovigilance System.
